title: Active learning selected antimicrobial polymer P7
summary: An automated Design-Build-Test-Learn campaign applied machine learning and high-throughput synthesis/characterization to a library of 13,728 polymer combinations. Across four active-learning rounds, the authors selected seven candidates for detailed testing. The leading polymer P7 had a reported MIC of 2 μg/mL and IC20 of 256 μg/mL, and was tested in in-vitro and animal models. These laboratory and preclinical results do not establish clinical efficacy or safety.
ai_technology: Graph Transformer model with active-learning selection
organization: Zhejiang University; Institute of Intelligent Chemical Manufacturing and iChemFoundry Platform, Zhejiang University

source_review.scope: Primary PMC indexed full text and NCBI/PubMed metadata/abstract for publication date, affiliations, model, assay outcomes and P7 result.

evidence.tested: The study reports seven top candidates from four active-learning rounds. P7 had MIC 2 μg/mL and IC20 256 μg/mL, with in-vitro characterization and animal-model testing reported by the authors.
evidence.unknown: These are laboratory and animal results, not human efficacy or safety. The entry reports the authors’ selection and assay result without a claim of global chemical novelty or clinical readiness.
evidence.ai_role: A graph-transformer prediction model and active-learning loop ranked polymer candidates for automated synthesis and antimicrobial/biocompatibility testing.
